## Hydrostatic and well-balanced evidence {#sec-ch15-ch05-tests}

### Summary

A balanced atmosphere should stay at rest, and it should stay at rest next to a wall and across a block seam as
well as in the interior. The tests of @sec-ch05 ask for that in two complementary ways: a residual that must be
small when a reference switch is on, and a deliberately unbalanced control that must stay large when it is
off, so that a misspelt or ignored switch cannot pass by accident. This section collects those tests, their
thresholds, and what a pass does and does not establish.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Ties the chapter 5 claims (reference clamp, wall order, fourth-order reference, centroid, balance, seams) to six registered tests.

**Data.** Rest residuals, two-grid orders and block-to-block gaps of the fixtures; thresholds read from the source.

**Placement.** Verification outside the simulation step, in a build at the code pin.

**Activation.** Select the tests by their ctest name; the Python tests run both switch arms in child processes.

**Guarantee / limits.** The thresholds separate the on and off arms; they are not round-off bounds.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch15-ch05-tests-assertions.
:::

Local symbols: none; the order estimate is the exponent $\zeta_{15}$ of
@eq-ch15-order and the rest residual is each test's own diagnostic.

The six tests fall into three groups: exact contracts of the reference (the wall clamp keeps ghosts out of the
interior; a split column matches one block), two-grid and three-grid orders of the near-wall and fourth-order
references, and rest residuals of the centroid correction and the balanced column.

### Derivation

Why the catalogue reads these tests the way it does, each step tied to the source at the pin.

1. *Run both arms, not one.* `main` of {{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py main >}} runs the fourth-order
   reference enabled and unset in child processes. A small rest residual in one arm would also pass if the
   switch were ignored; the control arm is what makes the test specific.
2. *Read an order from adjacent ratios.* The enabled arm requires every adjacent two-grid order of
   @eq-ch15-order to reach `ORDER_ON` $= 2.75$ over both doublings; the unset arm requires the last order to
   stay below `ORDER_OFF` $= 2.5$ ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py ORDER_ON >}},
   {{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py ORDER_OFF >}}). Near round-off a ratio stops measuring truncation; read
   the raw residuals against the bound of @sec-ch15 before reading the order.
3. *Read the near-wall row as a two-grid estimate.* `faces_next_to_the_walls_are_second_order`
   ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref_wall.cpp faces_next_to_the_walls_are_second_order >}}) requires the order from
   32 to 64 cells to be at least 1.7 and the reference error at the finer grid to be at most 1.5 times the
   largest interior error; two grids give one estimate, not an asymptotic order.
4. *Read the centroid row as a separation test.* `main` of {{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py main >}}
   requires the rest force below `TOL_ON` $= 10^{-10}$ with the centroid switch on, in the interior and at the
   walls, and above `TOL_OFF` $= 10^{-8}$ in the interior with it off
   ({{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py TOL_ON >}}, {{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py TOL_OFF >}}).
5. *Read the exact rows as exact.* `HydroRefX1Dispatch.wall_clamp_keeps_the_interior_free_of_the_ghosts`
   ({{< code tests/test_hydro_ref_x1.cpp HydroRefX1Dispatch.wall_clamp_keeps_the_interior_free_of_the_ghosts >}})
   compares the interior reference with and without perturbed ghosts by `torch::equal`.
   `BalanceColumn.a_moist_column_with_one_condensable_comes_out_at_rest`
   ({{< code tests/test_balance_column.cpp BalanceColumn.a_moist_column_with_one_condensable_comes_out_at_rest >}})
   requires the rest residual below $10^{-10}$, the species rows unchanged bit for bit and the temperature within
   $10^{-14}$. `HydroRefX1.in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps`
   ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp HydroRefX1.in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps >}})
   bounds the relative difference of four blocks against one after 200 steps by $10^{-12}$.

### Numerical method

Read the assertion and its registration, then run the selection in a build configured from the code pin
(@fig-ch15-evidence, @sec-ch15). The flux-covariance arm of the seam test is its own registration,
`test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance.release`, which sets `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1` and requires exactly one
passing case ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). Record device, precision, process count and every skip
separately.

: Assertions this catalogue reads. {#tbl-ch15-ch05-tests-sources}

**How to select the tests.** From the repository root, with `build` the directory configured from the code pin,
list the selection and then run it:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_wb_ref4_order_python$'
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R '^test_wb_ref4_order_python$'
```

The other rows are selected the same way:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_hydro_ref_x1\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_wb_ref_wall\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_x1_centroid_rest_python$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_balance_column\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance\.release$'
```

Run each listed selection with `--output-on-failure` in place of `-N`. Do not set `SNAP_WB_REF4` or
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` by hand for the Python rows: each script starts one child process per arm with the
variable set or unset, and a value inherited from the shell would make the control arm meaningless. An empty
selection prints "No tests were found!!!" and is not a result (@sec-ch15).

The contract of the order test, from `main` ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py main >}}):

```python
if switch and min(order) < ORDER_ON:
    failures.append(f"{n:g} e-folds, switch on: order {min(order):.2f} < {ORDER_ON}")
if not switch and not order[-1] < ORDER_OFF:
    failures.append(f"{n:g} e-folds, switch off: order {order[-1]:.2f} >= {ORDER_OFF}")
```

`order` holds the adjacent two-grid exponents of @eq-ch15-order over the resolutions; the on arm is judged on
its smallest, the off arm on its last.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_hydro_ref_x1.release` | the wall-clamped interior reference ignores perturbed ghosts | exact (`torch::equal`) | the test |
| `test_wb_ref_wall.release` | near-wall face errors shrink on refinement | order $\ge 1.7$; reference error $\le 1.5\times$ interior | the test |
| `test_wb_ref4_order_python` | the enabled reference converges at high order; the control does not | `ORDER_ON` $= 2.75$; `ORDER_OFF` $= 2.5$ | the script's constants |
| `test_x1_centroid_rest_python` | the centroid correction separates rest from the control | `TOL_ON` $= 10^{-10}$; `TOL_OFF` $= 10^{-8}$ | the script's constants |
| `test_balance_column.release` | a moist column balances without changing its species and stays at rest | residual $<10^{-10}$; species exact; $T$ within $10^{-14}$ | the test |
| `test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance.release` | four local blocks match one block after 200 steps | relative difference $\le10^{-12}$ | the test |

: Acceptance criteria at the code pin; CPU run evidence is recorded below, with CUDA coverage limited explicitly. {#tbl-ch15-ch05-tests-assertions}

The report-only `src/snapy_report/ch05/checks/wbref_check.py` checks the rational weights, the wall continuation, the
pressure source, the centroid and the balance iteration on ports and imports no snapy.

The enabled and unset arms together test whether the order oracle distinguishes the two reference paths.
The wall, centroid, balance and seam rows are separate contracts; passing one establishes none of the
others.[^ch15-ch05-run]

### Limits

The wall row compares two grids; a claim of asymptotic order needs at least three resolutions with the time
and solver errors controlled. This section adds no CPU, CUDA or distributed run of the well-balanced tests.
